findings.title: N+1 Query Pattern in get_by_topic
findings.description: The get_by_topic method iterates over memory IDs and calls self.get() for each one, resulting in N+1 database reads. Each get() call reads a file from disk independently.
findings.recommendation: Batch file reads by collecting all file paths first, then reading them in parallel using asyncio.gather or concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor.

findings.title: N+1 Query Pattern in get_by_entity
findings.description: Same N+1 pattern as get_by_topic - iterates over entity memory IDs and calls self.get() individually for each.
findings.recommendation: Implement batch file reading to reduce I/O operations.

findings.title: N+1 Query Pattern in search method
findings.description: When no entity_id or topics filter is provided, the search method iterates over ALL memory IDs and calls self.get() for each, causing severe performance degradation with large memory stores.
findings.recommendation: Implement indexed search or use a proper database query instead of loading all entries into memory. Consider adding FTS support for text search.

findings.title: N+1 Query in find_shortest_path BFS
findings.description: During BFS traversal, get_entity() is called for each neighbor node individually, causing multiple database queries per BFS level.
findings.recommendation: Batch load entities by collecting neighbor IDs at each BFS level, then fetch them in a single query using WHERE id IN (...).

findings.title: N+1 Query in get_subgraph
findings.description: After BFS traversal, entities and relationships are fetched one by one in separate loops, causing 2*N queries.
findings.recommendation: Use batch queries: SELECT * FROM entities WHERE id IN (...) and SELECT * FROM relationships WHERE id IN (...).

findings.title: N+1 Query in find_related_entities BFS
findings.description: Similar to find_shortest_path, get_entity() is called individually for each visited node during traversal.
findings.recommendation: Collect entity IDs during traversal, then batch fetch after BFS completes.

findings.title: O(n) Brute Force Vector Search Fallback
findings.description: When sqlite-vec is unavailable, _brute_force_search loads ALL vectors from the database and computes cosine similarity for each, resulting in O(n) complexity.
findings.snippet:
cursor.execute(sql, params)
for row in cursor:
    emb = np.frombuffer(row["embedding"], dtype=np.float32)
    score = float(np.dot(query_vector, emb) / (norm_q * norm_e))
findings.recommendation: Implement approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) fallback using libraries like faiss or annoy. At minimum, add LIMIT clause and early termination when enough high-score results are found.

findings.title: Sequential Execution in hybrid_search
findings.description: In the synchronous hybrid_search method, fuzzy_search and semantic_search are executed sequentially, doubling latency when both succeed.
findings.snippet:
fuzzy_results = self.fuzzy_search(query, top_k=top_k * 2, type_filter=type_filter)
semantic_results = self.semantic_search(query, top_k=top_k * 2, type_filter=type_filter)
findings.recommendation: Use concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor to run both searches in parallel, or always use the async search_async method which already uses asyncio.gather.

findings.title: Long-lived SQLite Connection Without Cleanup
findings.description: GraphManager creates a SQLite connection in __init__ that persists for the object lifetime. In long-running processes, this can lead to connection leaks if GraphManager instances are created but not properly closed.
findings.snippet:
self._conn: Optional[sqlite3.Connection] = None
self._lock = threading.RLock()
self._init_db()
findings.recommendation: Implement connection pooling or use context manager pattern consistently. Add __del__ method as safety net, or document that close() must be called.

findings.title: No Caching for Frequently Accessed Entities
findings.description: get_entity() always queries the database, even for the same entity_id accessed multiple times in quick succession (e.g., during graph traversal).
findings.recommendation: Add an LRU cache decorator or implement a simple in-memory cache with TTL for entity lookups, especially beneficial during graph traversal operations.

findings.title: Multiple COUNT Queries in get_entity_stats
findings.description: get_entity_stats executes 4 separate queries to collect statistics that could be combined into fewer queries.
findings.snippet:
cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entities")
cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM relationships")
cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT type, COUNT(*) FROM entities GROUP BY type")
cursor = self._conn.execute("SELECT type, COUNT(*) FROM relationships GROUP BY type")
findings.recommendation: Combine into 2 queries using UNION ALL or a single query with multiple CTEs. This reduces round-trips to the database.

findings.title: Full Directory Scan in _rebuild_index
findings.description: Index rebuild scans all directories recursively using nested loops (O(years * months * days * files)), which can be slow for large memory stores.
findings.recommendation: Use pathlib.glob('**/*.md') for simpler code, or implement incremental index updates to avoid full rebuilds.

findings.title: Synchronous Subprocess in _ripgrep_search
findings.description: ripgrep is executed synchronously with subprocess.run(), blocking the thread during file search operations.
findings.snippet:
proc = subprocess.run(
    cmd,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    timeout=10
)
findings.recommendation: Use asyncio.create_subprocess_exec for async execution, or run in a thread pool executor to avoid blocking the event loop.

findings.title: LIKE Query Without Index in Fallback Search
findings.description: _like_search uses LIKE '%term%' patterns which cannot use indexes and require full table scans.
findings.snippet:
conditions = [f"content LIKE ?" for _ in tokens]
params = [f"%{t}%" for t in tokens]
findings.recommendation: This is expected for LIKE with leading wildcards. Consider using FTS5 as primary search method and ensure it's always available, or implement trigram indexing for substring search.
